# Introduction

This document walks through a complete reserving workflow using NHBC's own data.

The data in Snowflake is not complete or fully validated yet. We have taken the ‘ClaimsData’ table from the NHBC Reserving database and uploaded it.

This table already has some data processing applied to it (including splitting it into capped and excess) and we have the query (currently in SQL code) to get to the manipulated data we use in our reserving models. 

As part of our planned development work in Reserving, we would like to be able to get to this data directly from the tables already in Snowflake. However, this is a process that is currently owned and run by the Data team and we haven’t yet had chance to work through these steps.

The data is available in `TEAM_SANDBOX.ACTUARIAL_RESERVING.CLAIMSDATA`.

The SQL query is shared as:

```python
if category == "Capped":
    sql_query = f"""
    SELECT c.Period,
           c.ReservingSegmentationGroup_Capped AS ReservingSegmentationGroup,
           c.UWY,
           c.FirstNotifiedFY,
           c.FirstNotifiedFYQuarter,
           c.ProcessingQuarter,
           SUM(c.ClaimCount) AS ClaimCount,
           SUM(c.Paid_Capped) AS Paid,
           SUM(c.CaseIncurred_Capped) AS Incurred,
           SUM(c.BuilderRecs_Capped) AS BuilderRecs
    FROM datastore.ClaimsData c
    WHERE c.Period = {xlPeriod.value}
      AND c.isExcludedReserving = 0
      AND c.UWY >= {xlUWYStart.value}
      AND c.ReservingSegmentationGroup_Capped = '{xlSegClass.value}'
      AND (
             c.ValidityIndicator = 'Y'
          OR c.Paid_Capped <> 0
          OR c.CaseIncurred_Capped <> 0
          OR c.BuilderRecs_Capped <> 0
      )
    GROUP BY c.Period, c.ReservingSegmentationGroup_Capped, c.UWY,
             c.FirstNotifiedFY, c.FirstNotifiedFYHalfYear, c.FirstNotifiedFYQuarter,
             c.FirstNotifiedMonth, c.ProcessingHalfYear, c.ProcessingQuarter, c.ProcessingMonth
    """
else:
    sql_query = f"""
    SELECT c.Period,
           c.ReservingSegmentationGroup_Excess AS ReservingSegmentationGroup,
           c.UWY,
           c.FirstNotifiedFY,
           c.FirstNotifiedFYQuarter,
           c.ProcessingQuarter,
           SUM(c.ClaimCount_Excess) AS ClaimCount,
           SUM(c.Paid_Excess) AS Paid,
           SUM(c.CaseIncurred_Excess) AS Incurred,
           SUM(c.BuilderRecs_Excess) AS BuilderRecs
    FROM datastore.ClaimsData c
    WHERE c.Period = {xlPeriod.value}
      AND c.isExcludedReserving = 0
      AND c.UWY >= {xlUWYStart.value}
      AND c.ReservingSegmentationGroup_Excess = '{xlSegClass.value}'
      AND (
             c.ValidityIndicator = 'Y'
          OR c.Paid_Excess <> 0
          OR c.CaseIncurred_Excess <> 0
          OR c.BuilderRecs_Excess <> 0
      )
    GROUP BY c.Period, c.ReservingSegmentationGroup_Excess, c.UWY,
             c.FirstNotifiedFY, c.FirstNotifiedFYHalfYear, c.FirstNotifiedFYQuarter,
             c.FirstNotifiedMonth, c.ProcessingHalfYear, c.ProcessingQuarter, c.ProcessingMonth
    """
```

## Sanity check on processing and first notified dates

Of course, you can't process a claim before it is notified, right?

```{python}
claims_data.filter(f.col("PROCESSINGQUARTER") < f.col("FIRSTNOTIFIEDFYQUARTER")).count() / claims_data.count()
```

Say, what?

> For the developments we use quarters and we just use the processing date data. But there is some nuance unfortunately. In the data provided to us (and you) the “ProcessingQuarter” is on a calendar year basis (for example, if a claim was processed in January 2020 this would appear in this column as 2020Q1). However, the UWY and first notified data are both on a financial year basis which runs April to March and by convention our current UWY is labelled as the year ending (i.e. we are currently in the 2026 UWY at NHBC). This means that when we’re building our triangles, we would treat the development quarter for a claim processed in Jan 2020 as 2020Q4.

## Correcting Processing Quarters

Let's make a function to convert to fiscal quarters. You will not have learnt how to make a user defined function on Snowflake from a python function yet so trust me or read up at:

<https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark/python/creating-udfs>

```{python}

from snowflake.snowpark.functions import udf
from snowflake.snowpark.types import StringType

## We NEED this set to declare and define the udf
session.use_database("TEAM_SANDBOX")
session.use_schema("ACTUARIAL_RESERVING")

@udf(return_type=StringType(), session=session)
def convert_calendar_to_fiscal_udf(calendar_quarter: str) -> str:
    year, qtr = calendar_quarter.split('Q')
    year = int(year)
    qtr = int(qtr)

    if qtr == 1:
        fiscal_qtr = 4
        fiscal_year = year
    else:
        fiscal_qtr = qtr - 1
        fiscal_year = year + 1

    return f"{fiscal_year}Q{fiscal_qtr}"
```

```{python}
claims_data = (
    claims_data
    .with_column(
        "ProcessingFYQuarter",
        convert_calendar_to_fiscal_udf(f.col("PROCESSINGQUARTER"))
    )
)
```

```{python}
claims_data.select("ProcessingQuarter", "ProcessingFYQuarter").sample(n = 50).to_pandas()
```

# Fiscal quarters to calendar dates

You are using quarterly developments which means you need to read carefully and understand

<https://github.com/casact/chainladder-python/discussions/545>

We need to understand that underwriting year is just a year but for reserving we essentially assume that all underwriting happens on the first day of the fiscal year, ie 1 April.

With this, we can now create columns in YYYY-MM-01 format for use with the chainladder package.

First, we define a function:

```{python}
#| label: fiscal_quarter_to_date_udf

from snowflake.snowpark.types import DateType
from datetime import datetime

@udf(name="fiscal_quarter_to_date", return_type=DateType(), input_types=[StringType()], session=session)
def fiscal_quarter_to_date_udf(fq_str: str) -> datetime:
    year, qtr = fq_str.split('Q')
    year = int(year)
    qtr = int(qtr)

    if qtr == 1:
        month = 4
        year -= 1
    elif qtr == 2:
        month = 7
        year -= 1
    elif qtr == 3:
        month = 10
        year -= 1
    elif qtr == 4:
        month = 1
        # year remains the same

    return datetime(year, month, 1)

```

Second, we use that to create dates for first notified and processing date. At the same time, we remember to convert underwriting year to a date.

```{python}
#| label: convert-fiscal-quarter-to-date

claims_data = (
    claims_data
    .with_columns(
        ["FirstNotified", "Processing", "UWD"],
        [
            fiscal_quarter_to_date_udf(f.col("FirstNotifiedFYQuarter")),
            fiscal_quarter_to_date_udf(f.col("ProcessingFYQuarter")),
            f.date_from_parts(f.col("UWY") - 1, 4, 1)
        ]
    )
)
```

Quick manual inspection:

```{python}
claims_data.select("FirstNotified", "FirstNotifiedFYQuarter", "Processing", "ProcessingFYQuarter", "UWD", "UWY").sample(n = 50).to_pandas()
```

Looking good!


# Write function to get aggregated data as per SQL query

We will write a function to get the same aggregated data as the SQL query, though we will of course use snowpark functions.

- [Snowpark developer guide](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark/python/index)
- [Snowpark API reference](https://docs.snowflake.com/developer-guide/snowpark/reference/python/latest/snowpark/index)

```{python}
#| label: get_aggregated_data
def get_aggregated_data(category, uwy_start, seg_class):
    """
    Function to filter and aggregate claims data based on the given category, UWY start, and segmentation class.

    Parameters:
    - category (str): Either "Capped" or "Excess".
    - uwy_start (int): The starting underwriting year.
    - seg_class (str): The segmentation class.

    Returns:
    - aggregated_data: The filtered and aggregated claims data.
    """
    if category not in ["Capped", "Excess"]:
        raise ValueError("Invalid category. Must be 'Capped' or 'Excess'.")

    if category == "Capped":
        if seg_class not in capped_groups["Groups"].to_list():
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid segmentation class '{seg_class}' for category 'Capped'.")
        filtered_data = (
            claims_data
            .filter((f.col("UWY") >= uwy_start) &
                    (f.col("ReservingSegmentationGroup_Capped") == seg_class) &
                    ((f.col("ValidityIndicator") == 'Y') |
                     (f.col("Paid_Capped") != 0) |
                     (f.col("CaseIncurred_Capped") != 0) |
                     (f.col("BuilderRecs_Capped") != 0)))
        )
        aggregated_data = (
            filtered_data
            .group_by("ReservingSegmentationGroup_Capped", "UWD", "UWY",
                      "FirstNotifiedFY", "FirstNotifiedFYHalfYear", "FirstNotifiedFYQuarter",
                      "FirstNotified", "ProcessingFYQuarter",
                      "FirstNotifiedMonth", "ProcessingHalfYear", "ProcessingQuarter", "ProcessingMonth", "Processing")
            .agg(
                f.sum("ClaimCount").alias("ClaimCount"),
                f.sum("Paid_Capped").alias("Paid"),
                f.sum("CaseIncurred_Capped").alias("Incurred"),
                f.sum("BuilderRecs_Capped").alias("BuilderRecs")
            )
            .select(
                f.col("ReservingSegmentationGroup_Capped").alias("ReservingSegmentationGroup"),
                f.col("UWD"),
                f.col("UWY"),
                f.col("FirstNotified"),
                f.col("FirstNotifiedFY"),
                f.col("FirstNotifiedFYQuarter"),
                f.col("Processing"),
                f.col("ProcessingQuarter"),
                f.col("ProcessingFYQuarter"),
                f.col("ClaimCount"),
                f.col("Paid"),
                f.col("Incurred"),
                f.col("BuilderRecs")
            )
        )
    else:  # category == "Excess"
        if seg_class not in excess_groups["Groups"].to_list():
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid segmentation class '{seg_class}' for category 'Excess'.")
        filtered_data = (
            claims_data
            .filter((f.col("UWY") >= uwy_start) &
                    (f.col("ReservingSegmentationGroup_Excess") == seg_class) &
                    ((f.col("ValidityIndicator") == 'Y') |
                     (f.col("Paid_Excess") != 0) |
                     (f.col("CaseIncurred_Excess") != 0) |
                     (f.col("BuilderRecs_Excess") != 0)))
        )
        aggregated_data = (
            filtered_data
            .group_by("ReservingSegmentationGroup_Excess", "UWD", "UWY",
                      "FirstNotifiedFY", "FirstNotifiedFYHalfYear", "FirstNotifiedFYQuarter",
                      "FirstNotified", "ProcessingFYQuarter",
                      "FirstNotifiedMonth", "ProcessingHalfYear", "ProcessingQuarter", "ProcessingMonth", "Processing")
            .agg(
                f.sum("ClaimCount_Excess").alias("ClaimCount"),
                f.sum("Paid_Excess").alias("Paid"),
                f.sum("CaseIncurred_Excess").alias("Incurred"),
                f.sum("BuilderRecs_Excess").alias("BuilderRecs")
            )
            .select(
                f.col("ReservingSegmentationGroup_Excess").alias('"ReservingSegmentationGroup"'),
                f.col("UWD"),
                f.col("UWY"),
                f.col("FirstNotified"),
                f.col("FirstNotifiedFY"),
                f.col("FirstNotifiedFYQuarter"),
                f.col("Processing"),
                f.col("ProcessingQuarter"),
                f.col("ProcessingFYQuarter"),
                f.col("ClaimCount"),
                f.col("Paid"),
                f.col("Incurred"),
                f.col("BuilderRecs")
            )
        )

    return aggregated_data

```

# ChainLadder package

First make aure you have installed the package using `uv add chainladder` from the terminal. Then load it as `cl`.

```{python}
#| label: import-chainladder
import chainladder as cl
```

We will be working with triangles and the user guide is here:

<https://chainladder-python.readthedocs.io/en/latest/getting_started/tutorials/triangle-tutorial.html>


## Creating the triangle

Let's do one by hand first. 

```{python}
#| label: pick-group-triangle
group = capped_groups[0, 'Groups']
group
```

First pick one of Capped / Excess and then pick one of the groups from there. I select `Capped` and `{python} group`.

Next, let's build the triangle data as in the previous exercise. Pick 2000 as the year.


```{python}
#| label: make-one-triangle
aggregate_data = get_aggregated_data("Capped", 2000, group)
triangle_data = (
    aggregate_data
    ## +++
    ## Use this for annual data
    .with_column(
        "Processing", f.substr(f.col("ProcessingFYQuarter"), 1, 4)
    )
    .with_column(
        "UWD", f.col("UWY").cast("string")
    )
    ## ---
    .group_by("UWD", "Processing")
    .agg(
        f.sum("ClaimCount").alias("ClaimCount"),
        f.sum("Paid").alias("Paid"),
        f.sum("Incurred").alias("Incurred")
    )
    .sort(f.col("UWD"), f.col("Processing"))
).to_pandas()
triangle_data = pl.from_pandas(triangle_data).rename({
    "CLAIMCOUNT": "ClaimCount",
    "PAID": "Paid",
    "INCURRED": "Incurred"
})
```

### Incomplete data

We need to deal with incomplete data for quarterly reserving.

First, find the full grid:

```{python}
#| eval: false
import datetime

min_uwd = triangle_data.select(pl.col("UWD").min()).item()
min_processing = triangle_data.select(pl.col("PROCESSING").min()).item()
max_uwd = triangle_data.select(pl.col("UWD").max()).item()
max_processing = triangle_data.select(pl.col("PROCESSING").max()).item()
last_complete_quarter = datetime.date(2025, 4, 1) # XXX FIXME

# Generate UWDs: annual on 1 April
start_year = min_uwd.year
end_year = max_uwd.year
uwd_dates = [datetime.date(year, 4, 1) for year in range(start_year, end_year + 1)]
uwd_df = pl.DataFrame({"UWD": uwd_dates})

# Generate Processing dates: quarterly on 1 April
start_date = min_processing
end_date = max_processing # last_complete_quarter # max_processing

processing_dates = []
current = start_date
while current <= end_date:
    processing_dates.append(current)
    month = current.month + 3
    year = current.year + (month - 1) // 12
    month = (month - 1) % 12 + 1
    current = datetime.date(year, month, 1)

processing_df = pl.DataFrame({"PROCESSING": processing_dates})

# Cartesian product and filter
full_grid = uwd_df.join(processing_df, how="cross")
valid_grid = full_grid.filter(pl.col("PROCESSING") >= pl.col("UWD"))
```

```{python}
# Perform left join
```

### Now make the triangle

Time to bring in chainladder:


```{python}

cl_triangle = cl.Triangle(
    #data=joined,
    data=triangle_data,
    origin="UWD",
    origin_format="yyyy-mm-dd",
    development="PROCESSING",
    development_format="yyyy-mm-dd",
    columns=["Paid", "Incurred", "ClaimCount"],
    cumulative=False
)
cl_triangle
```

```{python}
triangle_dt = cl.Pipeline(
```

# Memory


```{python}
from pympler import muppy, summary

# Get all objects in memory
```
